Reference / compression/brotli

compression/brotli#

Brotli (RFC 7932): what browsers ask for as Content-Encoding: br (#184).

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let packed = BrotliCompressed(data).bytes();
let data = BrotliDecompressed(origin: packed, limit: 10485760).bytes();

Description#

Brotli (RFC 7932): what browsers ask for as Content-Encoding: br (#184). Smaller than gzip on text, slower to compress at the high levels.

A stream goes through the Compressing and Decompressing roles, for example with compression/read:

let packed = CompressedReading(origin: input, compressor: BrotliCompressor());

Decompression is bounded: limit is the most bytes it may produce, past which it throws CompressionLimitExceeded; damaged data is InvalidCompressedData.

Public API#

object BrotliCompressed#

object BrotliCompressed

Bytes compressed whole; level 0 (fastest) to 11 (smallest and slowest), 11 unless told, as in the reference library. Web servers compressing on the fly usually take 4 to 6.

BrotliCompressed.BrotliCompressed#

BrotliCompressed(origin is @byte, level is int = 11)

Compresses origin whole as Brotli, at level 0 to 11 (11 unless told).

BrotliCompressed.bytes#

bytes() is @byte

The compressed bytes.

object BrotliDecompressed#

object BrotliDecompressed

Compressed bytes decompressed whole, at most limit bytes of them. Bytes after the end of the compressed stream are InvalidCompressedData.

BrotliDecompressed.BrotliDecompressed#

BrotliDecompressed(origin is @byte, limit is int)

Decompresses origin whole, producing at most limit bytes.

BrotliDecompressed.bytes#

bytes() is @byte

The decompressed bytes; more than limit is CompressionLimitExceeded, damaged data InvalidCompressedData.
